transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I really hope I'm not wasting your time. It's probably a fairly minor thing, but... well, what finally pushed me to make the appointment is that I just keep getting up during times when I really know I should stay put. 

Like, I'm a software developer, and during our long sprint planning meetings, or even on important personal calls—like I was on a mortgage call recently—I just... I leave my seat. I'll suddenly feel like I absolutely need to go grab a glass of water right that second, or I'll just decide to go check on something in the other room. I always try to be polite about it, of course, but I know I should just sit there like everyone else. Is that... does that make sense to come in for? I just don't want it to come across as unprofessional to my team, you know?

When you're sitting in these meetings or on important calls, do you feel physically restless or like you have excess energy that you need to get out—like fidgeting or needing to move around—or does it feel more like anxiety or worry about the situation itself that makes you want to leave?

Oh, um, no, it's definitely not anxiety about the work or the calls. I really like my job, and I'm totally comfortable with my team! It's... I guess it is more of a physical feeling? Like just a little bit of extra energy. 

I hope this doesn't sound too childish, but... well, in meetings, I'm almost always doing something small, like bouncing my knee or clicking a pen, or just shifting around in my chair. It's really minor, just little movements, I promise! But I honestly don't even notice how much I'm doing it until someone looks over at me, and then I feel awful because I really don't want to be a distraction to anyone else. Does that answer your question? I try to keep it as subtle as possible, but it just feels like my body wants to move.
How long have you been experiencing this restlessness and need to fidget or move around? Has this been something you've dealt with your whole life, or is it something that started more recently?

Um, well... I guess it's been a while? Like, probably my whole life, if I'm being honest. I hope that's okay to say. 

I mean, I can remember back in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes... well, they'd move my desk a little bit, or they'd have to remind me to stay in my seat. I was just really eager, you know? Like I'd pop up out of my chair, or I'd accidentally talk before they called on me. And sometimes I'd rush through my assignments, even when I totally understood the material, just because I wanted to get to the next thing. 

It wasn't that I was trying to be a bad kid or anything! I really wanted to be good. I just... I had a lot of energy back then, too. I try so much harder to keep it under control now, though. Is it normal for it to stick around this long? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than it is.

Beyond the fidgeting and restlessness you mentioned, do you find it difficult to concentrate or stay focused on tasks? For example, do you have trouble keeping your attention on one thing, or do you find your mind wandering easily, even when you're interested in what you're doing?

Um, well, I wouldn't say I have a *huge* problem with focus, really. I definitely don't want to sound like I'm not doing my job properly! I mean, I always get my work done, and I really do try my best. 

But, um... I guess sometimes my mind does wander just a tiny bit? Like, I'll sit down to review a pull request for work, or even when I was looking over those mortgage documents I mentioned, and I'll have the best intentions to just power through it. But then, maybe a few minutes later, I'll realize I've kind of just been staring at the same paragraph for a while. And my brain will have drifted off to, like, five completely unrelated things. 

It's not that I don't care about the work, I promise! It's just... a little blip in concentration, I suppose. I usually catch myself pretty quickly and get right back to it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope that makes sense. I really don't want it to seem like I'm just daydreaming all day.

When you're working on something that requires careful attention—like reviewing code or reading important documents—how often would you say you struggle to keep your focus? Is it happening multiple times a day, or is it more of an occasional thing that doesn't really interfere with getting your work done?

Um, well, it's... I guess it happens more often than I'd like to admit. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or not capable of doing my job, because I really do work hard! But, um, lately, it feels like it's happening a bit more frequently. Like, maybe a few times a day? 

It's just... well, it has started creating a tiny bit of friction, I suppose. At work, and even at home with my husband. It's nothing major, I promise! Just... people have had to follow up with me a little more than they used to on things I've missed or forgotten to finish. And it just makes me feel terrible, because I really worry that I'm becoming the unreliable one on the team, or the one who drops the ball when planning things at home. 

I'm trying so hard to stay on top of everything, I really am. I just... I don't want them to think I don't care. Do you think that's normal to struggle with that sometimes? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I still get things done eventually!

When you think about your typical day—at work, at home, with your husband—would you say the fidgeting and restlessness and needing to move around is more of a problem for you than the trouble focusing and your mind wandering, or do they feel about equally bothersome to you?

Um, well... I guess if I really had to compare them... maybe the moving around part is a little bit more noticeable? I hope that's the right way to answer that. 

I mean, the focus thing is definitely there, and I know I just said it causes some friction—which it does!—but I feel like I can usually hide it better? Like, if my mind wanders while I'm looking at my screens, nobody really knows except me. But with the fidgeting... it's just so much harder to keep still, you know? Like, I'm always kind of shifting in my chair, or bouncing my leg, or getting up to grab water when I don't really need it. My husband definitely notices when we're watching TV, and I'm always worried my coworkers can see me tapping my pen on Zoom calls. 

It just feels a bit more embarrassing, I guess? Like I'm being disruptive, even when I'm trying so hard not to be. But honestly, neither of them are completely ruining my life or anything! I really don't want to sound like I can't handle things. I just... I guess the physical restlessness is the one I have to actively fight against the most. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.

You mentioned your mind wandering a few times a day and sometimes forgetting things people have asked you to do. Looking back over the past few months or even years, would you say you've had significant problems with organization, losing track of important tasks, or forgetting appointments and commitments—or is that something that only happens occasionally?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's a *huge* problem. I mean, I definitely don't want you to think my life is just a complete mess! I really do try to stay on top of everything. I'm actually always writing things down to make sure I don't forget. 

It's just... I guess my system isn't always the most efficient? Like, I'll have my work tickets in one place, and then home repair notes on a sticky note, and budget reminders on my phone, and some things in Slack or email... and sometimes I feel like I spend a little more time trying to figure out what I was supposed to be doing than actually doing it. 

But I always figure it out eventually! I really do. It's not like I'm constantly missing major appointments or anything terrible like that. It's just a little bit scattered sometimes, I suppose. I hope that doesn't make me sound too disorganized. Do you think it's normal to have your notes kind of spread out like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

When you think about your work performance overall, would you say the trouble with focus and remembering things has actually caused you real problems—like missing deadlines, making mistakes, or needing to redo work—or is it more just a minor inconvenience that you manage around?

Oh, um, no! Definitely not real problems like that. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm doing a bad job or anything! I mean, I take my work very seriously. I don't really miss deadlines or make big mistakes that I have to completely redo. 

It's really just... well, exactly like you said, more of a minor inconvenience that I just manage around. I might have to double-check my code an extra time or two just to be absolutely sure I didn't miss a line, but I always get it done on time! Everyone has to review their work sometimes, right? I just put in a little extra effort to make sure everything is correct before I submit it, so nobody is disappointed in me. 

I hope that makes sense? I really am doing okay with the actual work part, I promise. I just don't want to sound like I'm incapable of doing my job!

You've mentioned that your mind wanders a few times a day and you sometimes need to double-check your work. When that happens, how much does it actually bother you or get in your way compared to the restlessness and fidgeting? In other words, if you had to pick one to focus on fixing, which one would feel more important to address?

Oh, um... wow, that's a really good question. I'm honestly not entirely sure? I hope it's okay to say that! I just... I don't really want to make a huge deal out of either of them, because I really am doing okay overall. 

If I absolutely had to pick one... I guess I'd probably stick with what I mentioned earlier about the physical restlessness? Just because that's the one that feels like it might bother *other* people, or at least makes me worry that they're noticing it. The mind wandering and having to double-check my work... I mean, it's a little annoying sometimes, sure, but it really only affects me. I can always just put in a little extra time to make up for it so nobody else has to deal with the consequences, you know? 

So I suppose the fidgeting would be the one I'd want to fix first, just so I don't risk being disruptive or looking unprofessional to anyone else. Is that a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much about things I can just work through on my own!

You mentioned that your husband has noticed the fidgeting and your coworkers might see it—has anyone ever expressed concern about your organization, forgetfulness, or the way you handle tasks and responsibilities at home or at work in a way that's actually caused problems between you?

Oh, um... well... I wouldn't say there are *major* problems, really. My husband is super supportive, and my coworkers are great. I definitely don't want to make it sound like everyone is mad at me all the time! 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't sound too awful—there has been a little bit of... friction, maybe? Lately, anyway. It's just that I think people are having to follow up with me a bit more often than they used to. Like, at work, someone might have to ping me to ask about a ticket status, or at home, my husband might have to remind me about something we were supposed to plan. 

I really am trying so hard, though! I don't want anyone to think I don't care. It just worries me sometimes that I might be turning into the "unreliable one" when it comes to planning things or keeping track of tasks. I really hate the idea of letting anyone down. Do you think it's normal to feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without making it sound worse than it actually is.

When your husband or coworkers have to follow up with you about things, how much does that actually frustrate them, or have they said it's becoming a real problem for them—or do they seem pretty understanding about it?

Oh, um... well, they're mostly very understanding! I really am lucky to have such patient people around me. I don't want you to think they're constantly angry with me or anything like that. 

But, I mean... I guess I have noticed that it's starting to create just a little bit of friction? Like, maybe they get a tiny bit frustrated when they have to check in on me more than they used to. I can tell my husband gets a little exasperated when he has to ask me again about something we were supposed to plan, and at work, I just... I really worry that they're starting to see me as the unreliable one when it comes to organizing tasks. 

I really am trying my absolute hardest, I promise! I don't want them to feel like they have to manage me. It's just... it's been a bit harder lately, and I hate thinking that I'm becoming a burden or that they're disappointed in me. I hope I'm not making it sound like a huge crisis, because we're all still getting along fine! I just... I want to be someone they can always count on, you know? Does that make sense?

When you think about the times your mind wanders or you have to double-check your work—would you say that's actually causing real problems in your life, or is it something you can pretty easily manage and work around without it really affecting your job performance or your relationships?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say it's causing *real* problems. I really don't want it to sound like I'm failing at my job or anything! I always manage to get things done eventually. 

It's just... I guess it's a little embarrassing to admit, but sometimes I'll sit down with all the right intentions, you know? Like, I'll pull up a pull request to review at work, or at home I'll sit down to look over some mortgage documents we need to sign. And I really mean to focus! But then... I don't know, a few minutes go by, and I suddenly realize I've just been staring at the exact same paragraph the whole time, and my brain is off thinking about five completely unrelated things. 

I can usually catch myself and just start over, so I don't think it's ruining anything. It just takes a little extra effort to get through things sometimes. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely incompetent! I really do try to stay on top of it. Does that sound like a normal thing that happens to people?

You mentioned you catch yourself and start over, and that you always get things done eventually. But when you have to go back and re-read things or double-check your work, how much extra time does that actually add to your day? Are we talking about a few extra minutes here and there, or is it taking up a noticeable chunk of your time?

Oh, um... well, it's definitely not taking up a huge chunk of my day! I mean, I really wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting there wasting hours and hours. I'm still getting my work done and meeting my deadlines, I promise. 

It's probably just... you know, a few extra minutes here and there. Like, maybe I have to read a sentence twice, or I just take a little longer to finish reviewing a document than someone else might. It's really not a big deal at all! I just kind of power through it, and I think I manage it pretty well. I mean, everyone gets a little distracted sometimes and has to re-read things, right? I'm sure that's completely normal. I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and not making a mountain out of a molehill!

I want to go back to something you mentioned earlier. You said people have had to follow up with you more often lately, and your husband has to remind you about things. When that happens, does it actually create real problems or tension between you two, or is it more just a minor annoyance that you all work through?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't call it tension, really! He's wonderful about it, honestly. We don't fight about it or anything like that. It's really just a minor annoyance, if anything at all. 

I guess... well, sometimes if he asks me to do a few things in a row, like if he says, "Hey, can you call the insurance company, upload that form, and then email me the confirmation?"... I'll get right on it! I always do the first part right away. It's just that, occasionally, that very last step—like sending the email—just sort of... slips my mind for a bit. And it just sits there unfinished until he gently reminds me. 

But once he does, I do it immediately! I really don't want you to think I'm ignoring him or dropping the ball completely. It's just a little hiccup with finishing that final piece sometimes. I'm sure that happens to everyone when they're juggling a lot, right? I just hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is!

When you think about how these things—the mind wandering, the fidgeting, the needing to double-check your work, and people having to follow up with you—add up over time, would you say they're actually getting in the way of your ability to do your job well or affecting your relationship with your husband, even if it's just a little bit? Or do you feel like you're managing everything just fine overall?

Oh, um... well, I really wouldn't say it's completely getting in the way or anything! I'm still doing my job, and my husband and I have a great relationship, I promise. I don't want to make it sound like my life is falling apart. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has started creating just a tiny bit of friction lately. Nothing major! Just... well, at work and at home, people are having to follow up with me a little more than they used to. And it does worry me sometimes. I mean, I try so hard, I really do! But I get this awful feeling that I'm starting to become the "unreliable one" when it comes to planning things or finishing tasks. 

I really don't want people to think I don't care, because I do. I'm trying my absolute best to keep everything running smoothly. It's just a little harder than it used to be, I suppose. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like I'm just making excuses for myself. It's normal to worry about letting people down, isn't it?

When you were younger—back in elementary school or middle school—did you also have trouble keeping your attention on things, or was it mainly just the restlessness and fidgeting that teachers noticed back then?

Oh, um... well, I don't think I had a hard time paying attention, really! I was a good student, I promise, and I always understood the material. I guess it was... well, mostly the restlessness that they noticed back then. 

I remember a few of my elementary school teachers actually had to move my desk a couple of times, or they'd have to gently remind me to stay seated. I was just... always popping up out of my chair, you know? And sometimes I'd get a little too eager and talk before I was called on. Or I'd kind of just rush through my assignments, even though I knew how to do the work perfectly well! I just wanted to get to the next thing, I guess. 

But I really wasn't trying to be a troublemaker or anything! I just had a lot of enthusiasm. It's pretty normal for kids to be a bit chatty and full of energy like that, isn't it? I just hope I wasn't too much of a handful for my teachers!

When you were in elementary school, besides the restlessness and popping out of your seat, do you remember your teachers ever expressing concern about you not paying attention, getting distracted, or having trouble focusing on lessons—or was it really just the fidgeting and eagerness that was the main issue they noticed?

Oh, no, I really don't think they ever worried about my focus! I mean, I don't remember them ever saying I wasn't paying attention. I was always following along with the lessons, really! 

It was definitely just the... the extra energy, I guess you'd call it. The popping up, the chatty stuff. I never got in trouble for daydreaming or staring out the window or anything like that. I was very present! I just... maybe I was a little too present sometimes? Like, I just couldn't wait to participate. 

But as far as getting distracted or losing focus, no, I don't think that was ever an issue. I'm pretty sure I was a very attentive student, overall. That's a good thing, right? I mean, it shows I cared about school!
